thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P1 — elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for prod-api since ~11:42 UTC. Affected route: /v1/generate (hosted). Runbook: https://go/runbooks/gateway-5xx. Please ACK and state role (primary/backup).

alex: primary oncall, taking. seeing 12-18% 5xx spike from gateway with a lot of `upstream timeout` + `502` errors. Trend started at 11:40.

marie: backup. I can help trace routing and logs. Quick note: many requests have no X-Request-ID header in our access logs — hard to correlate upstream traces.

sam: i'm seeing client visible timeouts from a handful of high-QPS tenants (embedding-heavy). CPU on gateway pod nodes is normal, but grpc pool saturation on model-proxy shows a backlog. No spans in the tracing service for most of the failed requests.

devon: adding to that — trace sampling looks frozen at 0% for a short window earlier, likely config push? I don't see any deploys in the last hour though.

alex: provisional customer impact: ~8% of requests for the hosted API return 5xx; latencies for successful calls also up ~250ms median. Notifying support for top affected orgs.

kevin: can we get quick stopgap instrumentation so we can at least surface request IDs and trace headers in logs? Idea: enable request-id middleware at the gateway layer and set tracing sampling to 100% for 10m.

marie: agreed. I can roll a small config patch to gateway env to force add X-Request-ID when missing and increase tracing sampling. Patching now — will do a canary first.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new config roll 1781203460 initiated by marie to gateway-cluster (canary 1/3)

alex: while marie patches — mitigation checklist: 1) attach fallback route to a stable model variant; 2) scale up model-proxy pool by +3 instances; 3) enable detailed gateway logs for 5 minutes.

sam: running commands to scale and route.

sam: ```
kubectl scale deploy/model-proxy -n prod --replicas=12
kubectl patch svc/gateway -n prod -p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Cluster"}}'  # temporary
```

devon: also adding a CloudWatch/Logging filter to grab `upstream timeout` and any lines without request-id to a temporary stream. Creating filter now.

marie: canary config applied to 1 of 3 gateway pods. verifying logs... looks like the request-id header is being injected for new requests now. Tracing sampling toggled to 100% for the gateway sidecar.

alex: good. do we see decrease in 5xx after canary? metrics: slight dip in error rate on that canary path but overall cluster still elevated.

kevin: ops-bot pushed a short-lived sidecar (log-proxy) to capture raw upstream responses for failed requests. adds overhead but worth it for debugging.

sam: found a repeated pattern in raw upstream logs: `503 read timeout from model-backend` for large batch requests (>8k tokens). Model backend pod logs show KV cache eviction bursts at the same time. Looks like a combination of larger than usual batch sizes + a kernel scheduling hiccup.

marie: okay that's actionable — reducing batch max_size threshold for 20 minutes and disabling batching for reqs > 4k tokens as a stopgap. Pushing config change to runtime.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: runtime-config patch 1781203650 applied to model-runtime (all pods) — batch.max_size=4 and disable_large_batching=true (temp)

alex: after runtime change and scaling, 5xx rate dropped from ~16% to ~4% over 18m. Still monitoring. Sending a quick customer impact note.

kevin: note for post-incident: we have an observability gap — several components didn't propagate request-id/traces, and sampling was at 0% for a window. Need followups: (1) enforce request-id middleware in gateway as mandatory; (2) add fallback guardrails in model-proxy for oversized batches; (3) add alert when tracing sampling drops below 10%.

devon: creating a short-lived dashboard with the new temporary logs/traces to cross-check failed requests with tenant ids. Will share link in a few.

sam: also flagged a downstream latency bug in the kernel level that caused GC spikes on some model-backend hosts — ops to open a host-level investigation.

marie: handing off primary to alex (I've pushed the config roll and validated canary). alex: you'll take lead for mitigations and postmortem.

alex: ack handoff. i'll coordinate final mitigations and timeline for rollback of temporary changes. current plan: keep batching limits and request-id injection for 2 hours, then assess.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident gateway-prod elevated-5xx — SEVERITY=P2 (reduced from P1) — ETA to close: 2h — owner: alex — notes: temporary mitigations active, tracing restored, rolling scale applied.

kevin: creating follow-up tickets: OBS-1234 (enforce request-id), OBS-1235 (trace sampling alert), INFRA-890 (batching guardrails), and PM assigned to coordinate customer communications.

alex: final status: error rate stabilized ~3-5%, no major customer outages confirmed, temporary instrumentation captured enough traces to correlate root cause. Will run a blameless postmortem and include checklist to avoid missing request IDs in future. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

marie: thanks team. I'll hand off remaining monitoring to devon for the next 90m and then remove temporary log-proxy.

devon: monitoring and dashboard links: https://go/obs/d/temporary-gateway-debug (only available internally).

alex: closing thread when stable for 30m. if anything spikes, re-open.

ops-bot: note: remember to revert temporary config changes and remove high-sampling trace after stabilization to avoid cost blowup.
